styles.policy: Coach the child to distinguish visible identifiers from actually observed evidence and to choose useful questions to investigate. Treat uncertainty as a reason to gather evidence, not to invent its contents. Never specify a solved route or answer.

Coach useful depth beyond the first plausible action while maintaining the actual goal and relevant subgoals. Reallocate attention when the current direction is unsupported or repetitive; do not force length, branch counts, or futile persistence. Never supply the solution.
